followup_explanation:
This was a source-based extraction and synthesis task — pulling evidence from provided primary sources and a video clip to answer a well-specified history question with clear completion criteria. That kind of work plays to Extraction & Retrieval and Summarization strengths.

I routed to Willet-235B primarily because its capability profile is stronger across the board: Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 79.2) and Summarization (86.4 vs 80.6) both favor Willet by margins well outside the run-to-run variance threshold, and its general benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, IFEval) are higher too. Since this is an academic, source-grounded task, those capability advantages matter directly.

The task-preference notes weren't a deciding factor here — Lapwing actually self-reports *liking* well-specified retrieval/extraction tasks like this one, but its documentation explicitly notes that preference is dissociated from capability. Willet's preference profile (flat response to fraught content) is irrelevant to a benign history assignment. So the choice came down to raw capability on the relevant eval dimensions, where Willet leads.
